neighbours.label: the auxiliary / adverb slot right before an expected 'known/knew/know' in 'what X have long ▁known' frames (… confirmed what teachers have ▁, we both ▁); the output promotes ' know'
fire: The report confirms what farmers have known for generations: healthy soil holds more water.
The new data only prove what most pilots already know about fatigue.
The trial showed what many parents have long suspected about sugar.
Scientists have finally measured what sailors have known for centuries.
The audit revealed what the staff had already known for months.
The poll confirmed what the campaign has always known about rural voters.
It was a pointless excuse, and they both knew it.
The verdict affirmed what her neighbours had known all along.
quiet: The farmers have grown wheat on this soil for generations.
Most pilots already fly more than eighty hours a month.
Many parents have long served sugar-free snacks after school.
Sailors have crossed this strait for centuries.
The staff had already left the building for the night.
The campaign has always spent heavily on rural radio.
It was a small cake, and they both ate it.
Her neighbours had lived on the street all their lives.

notes: Card: peaks on ' have', ' already', ' both', ' always', ' been' before known/knew/suspected/acknowledged; logit effect promotes know/known/knew. Probes: 'what teachers have' 0.90, 'what most nurses already' 0.79, 'what I have (always suspected)' 0.63, 'we both (knew)' 0.36; 'teachers have worked' 0.07, 'We both ate' 0.05, 'already work' 0.22.
